chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “In the bathhouse, the junub and others bathe in it; may I bathe from its water?” He said: “Yes, there is no harm in the junub bathing from it. I have indeed bathed in it, then I came and washed my feet, and I only washed them because of the dirt that had stuck to them.”

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.مِنْ مَائِهِ: from its water, meaning the bathhouse water
key_terms.ٱلتُّرَابِ: dirt or soil clinging to the feet
key_terms.ٱلْجُنُبُ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.ٱلْحَمَّامُ: the bathhouse or public bathing place

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to bathe with bathhouse water used by a junub?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that using the water of a bathhouse in which a junub and others have bathed is permissible. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام clarifies that there is no problem in such bathing, and his washing of the feet afterward was only due to attached dirt, not because the water was considered impure.
